ledger.what: remove cookie/consent chrome (OneTrust, Cookiebot, Usercentrics, generic cookie-banner ids/classes)
ledger.why: overlay chrome injected by a CMP, not page content; re-added at deploy time

ledger.what: de-carousel slick/swiper/splide/glide: remove clone slides, force real slides visible+static, drop dots/arrows
ledger.why: hidden slides are absent from innerText and clones duplicate it — rotating carousels break byte determinism; the reskin renders all slides statically in DOM order

ledger.what: flatten the scroll-choreography stage: scroll every .sc-group/.sc-layer into view once so lazily-built blocks (chapters.migrate, install) decorate, then force every parked/waiting layer visible (visibility/opacity/display) and settle reveal/scramble animations
ledger.why: the live page parks off-screen layers with visibility:hidden, so innerText depends on scroll position (3168 chars at load, 848–3729 while scrolling); un-parking gives a deterministic reading-order reference with every authored chapter present. Presentation-only — no node is removed
progress-rail decoration that duplicates the chapter names ("REDESIGN", "Migrate as is") as a scroll indicator — duplication, not content

ledger.what: finish the install terminal typewriter by clicking its own [data-skip] control (the block removes the skip button and writes the full script)
ledger.why: the terminal types the authored script at random 14–54ms per key on reveal — innerText is time-dependent mid-typing; skip is the block's own deterministic end state. The "skip" label is transient UI, not content
USER-REQUESTED CONTENT REMOVAL (2026-10-11, "remove the version above the H1"). Not chrome — an explicit owner decision, recorded here so capture and gate exclude it identically

ledger.what: remove the spotlight route diagram (.spotlight .spot-media — labels: extract direct prototype migrate replica deploy rollout)
ledger.why: USER-REQUESTED CONTENT REMOVAL (2026-10-11, "Two ways in." section: remove the route diagram). Owner decision; capture and gate exclude it identically
USER-REQUESTED CONTENT REMOVAL (2026-10-11, "remove the stardust chip above the H1 to make more space for the demo"). The brand stays in the nav; capture and gate exclude it identically

ledger.what: remove the chapter intro titles (.chapters .sc-title — "Redesign", "Migrate as is") next to their [TAB] labels
ledger.why: USER-REQUESTED CONTENT REMOVAL (2026-10-11, "just say REDESIGN in square brackets"); applied to both chapter intros for consistency. The tab label carries the same word
USER-REQUESTED CONTENT REMOVAL (2026-10-12, "remove SCROLL which is useless"). Owner decision

ledger.what: COPY EDIT of the hero kicker first line: "Takes a website. Brings it back" -> "Takes a website & brings it back," (rev 17 wording; only when the old string is present)
ledger.why: USER-REQUESTED COPY CHANGE (2026-10-12). Not yet on the live source: until the stardust.style hero is re-authored, the live page still reads the old line. Guarded, so it becomes a no-op once the source carries the new copy

ledger.what: remove the install credit line (.install .credit — "Built on impeccable.")
ledger.why: USER-REQUESTED CONTENT REMOVAL (2026-10-12, "remove mentions that stardust is built on impeccable — that has been reducing over time"). Owner decision

ledger.what: remove the impeccable lines from the install terminal (.install .terminal pre span containing "impeccable": the marketplace add, the install command, and the "installed impeccable · design craft" reply)
ledger.why: USER-REQUESTED CONTENT REMOVAL (2026-10-12, "remove impeccable from the install demo too"). Runs after N3 finished the typewriter. Owner decision

ledger.what: COPY EDIT of the install heading second line: "Then ask it." -> "Docs included." (guarded on the old string)
ledger.why: USER-REQUESTED COPY CHANGE (2026-10-12): heading becomes "Install it. Docs included." Not on the live source until re-authored

ledger.what: COPY EDIT of the install lede -> "Stardust is a set of AI skills. Install it, then say what you want in your own words." (guarded on the exact old paragraph)
ledger.why: USER-REQUESTED COPY CHANGE (2026-10-12); drops the impeccable/Playwright dependency sentence and "Slash commands are optional." Not on the live source until re-authored

ledger.what: COPY EDIT of the "Two ways in." lede: drop the trailing sentence " Or open a door yourself." (guarded on the exact old paragraph)
ledger.why: USER-REQUESTED COPY CHANGE (2026-10-12). Not on the live source until re-authored

ledger.what: CONTENT ADDITION in the "Migrate as is" door: clone the Redesign door's Shortcut label + command paragraphs and set the command to "/stardust:replica <url>", inserted before "Follow the migration"
ledger.why: USER-REQUESTED ADDITION (2026-10-12, "put a shortcut like in the redesign box: /stardust:replica <url>"). Cloned from the source's own elements so markup/casing match. Not on the live source until re-authored

visibleTextNormalized: Takes a website & brings it back, redesigned, fixed, migrated. Or all three. SEED md5("brand" · 2026-10-12) → 734513cd · yours alone, today only Redesign the Web. Two ways in. Say what you want in a sentence and the master skill picks the route. Redesign New design on the site you have. extract → direct → prototype → migrate A B SHORTCUT /stardust:uplift <url> one URL, three pitch variants, one cinematic FOLLOW THE REDESIGN Migrate as is Same design, new platform. replica → deploy → rollout A B SHORTCUT /stardust:replica <url> FOLLOW THE MIGRATION REDESIGN Take a live site. Bring it back redesigned. Three skills, three steps. Each writes its files and the next one reads them. Or say what you want in a sentence and the master skill picks the route. “You can go from global brand to regionalized site in Edge Delivery Services in under a day.” A guest on Thursday Frequency · aem-live live session, 18 June 2026 0 1 Extract /stardust:extract <url> Read the site you already have. Point it at a URL. Stardust renders each page in a real browser and writes down the palette, the type scale, the motifs, the voice and every block of copy. Five pages by default, the whole site on request. It invents nothing at this stage. The capture is the evidence the next steps argue from. https://www.example.com/ 5 pages BRAND SURFACE Aa serif display 1.25 scale radius 12px voice: assured 5 pages gradient blob hero IN THIS STEP Real browser render, not view-source Palette, type scale, motifs, voice Every line of copy, counted PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md as output Read extract on GitHub 0 2 Direct /stardust:direct One sentence in. A direction out. Tell it what you want in plain words: warmer, more editorial, keep our type. Direct reads the capture, keeps your palette and fonts unless you ask for a rebrand, researches references when it can, and rolls the seed for whatever is still open. It writes the target spec and its reasoning, so you can argue with it. /stardust:direct seed · 2026-10-12 MD5("EXAMPLE.COM" · TODAY) a3f7c92e 8b1d488a 0c5ef691 3427bbd1 → resolves to decade 1970s a3 craft letterpress f7 register editorial c9 ground inherited — IN THIS STEP Brand-faithful by default, rebrand on request References first, seed for the rest Decade, craft, register from the roll A target spec and its reasoning trace Read direct on GitHub 0 3 Prototype /stardust:prototype Before and after, side by side. Prototype renders one page of the redesign as a single HTML file and puts it next to the capture. Then it runs impeccable's craft loop: critique, audit, adapt to six viewports, check the motion. It rejects template-looking output. You pick, annotate, and re-run. Approve it, and migrate carries the design to every page as static HTML. BEFORE AFTER 6 viewports IN THIS STEP Critique, audit, adapt, motion Checked at six viewports Optional cinematic motion register Approve, then migrate to every page Read prototype on GitHub Frescopa, before and after. White-label demo site. Redesigned with extract, direct, prototype. HOW IT WAS MADE FRESCOPA · BEFORE FRESCOPA · AFTER MIGRATE AS IS Keep the design. Change the platform. Same site, new origin. Replica rebuilds it as clean HTML and proves the match. Deploy and rollout carry it to AEM Edge Delivery, one page first, then the whole site. When one site becomes many markets, with in-place authoring, drafts, translations and scheduled releases, this is the route to production. “The ROI on being able to do that... it's undeniable.” Thursday Frequency, aem-live Static HTML every page, tokens, provenance · any host stardust:deploy one page → EDS blocks + authorable content AEM Edge Delivery rollout the site · qa the live pages 0 1 Replica /stardust:replica <url> The site you have, rebuilt clean. Replica reads the live site and recreates one page per template as clean HTML and CSS, never a DOM copy. It gates each one against the original at two breakpoints: structure, visuals, a stitched pixel diff. The only design changes allowed are the ones you list. Then migrate clones the rest of the pages. gate · 2 breakpoints diff < 2% ✓ LIVE REPLICA structure ✓ visuals ✓ pixel diff ✓ IN THIS STEP One archetype per page type Clean HTML and CSS, no DOM copy Pixel diff gate at two breakpoints migrate clones the sibling pages Read replica on GitHub 0 2 Deploy /stardust:deploy One page into blocks. Deploy takes one page of static HTML and turns each section into an Edge Delivery block with its own CSS, and the copy into authorable content. It writes both through the Document Authoring API, previews, publishes, then reads the live page back and checks it. A page counts as deployed only when that check passes. index.html → blocks preview · publish · check hero cards text quote IN THIS STEP Each section becomes one block Copy stays editable in Document Authoring Internal links rewritten to the new origin Live page checked before it counts Read deploy on GitHub 0 3 Rollout /stardust:rollout The whole site, then the check. Rollout runs deploy across the migrated tree. It keeps a ledger of what shipped and what is left, shares blocks across pages instead of forking them, adds the sitemap and redirects, and audits every link. When it is done, qa sweeps the live site and reports what it finds. It never edits. stardust/rollout/ledger.json delivered 112 / 134 / DELIVERED /about DELIVERED /products DELIVERED /products/beans DELIVERED /news/2026 DEPLOYING /contact PENDING shared blocks ✓ · sitemap ✓ · redirects ✓ · links ✓ IN THIS STEP A ledger of shipped and pending pages Blocks shared, not forked per page Sitemap, redirects, link audit qa reports on the live site Read rollout on GitHub Install it. Docs included. Stardust is a set of AI skills. Install it, then say what you want in your own words. COPY INSTALL README ON GITHUB “One of the most incredible open source skills I've ever seen.” Thursday Frequency, aem-live ~/project ~/project › /plugin marketplace add adobe/skills /plugin install stardust@adobe-skills installed stardust 0.20.0 · 14 skills ~/project › /stardust make example.com feel like a magazine, keep our type reading example.com · 5 pages brand-faithful mode · palette and type pinned decade ✓ rolled → 1970s craft ✓ rolled → letterpress plan written to stardust/direction.md · confirm to run
